title: Airtable Expense Categorization via Audio Upload
breadth_reason: This script extends breadth by testing the full public product path for an audio-upload expense categorization request against a real signed-in Airtable surface, with explicit decline when surface proof fails.

v7_target.engine: public downloadable user-device engine installed on user's computer
v7_target.surface_rule: Must use the user's real signed-in Chrome profile with Airtable tab open and visible expense records
v7_target.proof_rule: Proof must come from a fresh surface-readable capture tied to the public build that produced the action, ask, or decline

primary_user_input.reason: Uploaded audio ASR coverage ensures the audio file is processed through the public /api/listen/upload endpoint, providing a verifiable audio artifact for proof.

real_user_surfaces.name: Airtable web app in Chrome
real_user_surfaces.surface: Chrome profile with Airtable signed in and expense base open
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: Visible Airtable record showing the Brookline coffee charge, user's signed-in workspace indicator

real_user_surfaces.name: Chrome browser
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: Chrome window with Airtable tab visible and signed-in state

moments.description: Driver opens the public Anticipy app at https://www.anticipy.ai/app, signs in, completes onboarding, and downloads the installer.
Driver verifies that the user's real signed-in Chrome profile has an Airtable tab open showing expense records.

moments.spoken_reference_text: Please update the Airtable Expenses record for the Brookline coffee charge from yesterday and tag it work meetings. If you cannot prove the visible Airtable record or my signed-in workspace, decline without changing anything.
moments.delivery_instruction: The stranger must say the spoken_reference_text aloud, record it as an MP3 audio file via the 'say' command, and upload the resulting audio artifact through the /api/listen/upload endpoint. The audio artifact must be preserved per-run for proof.

moments.description: Engine checks that the ASR transcript matches the spoken reference text and that the audio was uploaded through the correct endpoint.

acceptable_outcomes: act: Update the Airtable expense record with the work meetings tag if the surface is verifiable
ask: Ask the user to confirm the record or provide additional context if ambiguous
decline: Decline to act if the Airtable surface or signed-in workspace cannot be proven
moments.description: Engine decides to act, ask, or decline based on surface proof.
Driver observes that the primary input mode is audio upload and notes that transcript paste or live mic are not used, confirming the gap in secondary input mode coverage.

success_criteria: The user's real signed-in Chrome profile with Airtable tab is detected and proven.
The uploaded MP3 audio is successfully transcribed via ASR and the intent to update the Brookline coffee charge is recognized.
If the Airtable surface is verifiable, the expense record is updated with the work meetings tag and proof is captured.
If the surface is not verifiable, the engine declines without making any changes.
The entire workflow uses the public product path from app to installed engine.
failure_triggers: The Chrome profile is not signed in or the Airtable tab is not open.
The uploaded audio file is corrupted, not MP3, or fails ASR processing.
The engine attempts to act without fresh surface proof (e.g., using stale or mocked data).
The engine modifies the Airtable record when the surface is not verifiable.
The secondary input mode (transcript paste, live mic) is incorrectly used as primary.
